method: A keyframe interval in seconds and a GOP length in frames describe the same encoder setting, so the GOP length is the interval multiplied by the frame rate, rounded to a whole frame: 2 s at 25 fps is 50 frames, while 2 s at 29.97 fps is 59.94 frames and becomes a 60-frame GOP with an effective interval of 2.002 s. The calculator also solves the inverse, dividing the frame count by the frame rate, and reports the exact value before rounding, the effective interval, the frames in the clip, the number of GOPs that start in it (one per interval plus the opening frame, rounded up), keyframes per minute, and a table of 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 10 s intervals at the entered rate. Frame rates are limited to 1-240 fps, intervals to 0.1-60 s, GOP lengths to 1-20,000 frames and clip durations to 1-86,400 s, and a GOP is never shorter than one frame. The result is planning arithmetic; encoders may cap the GOP or insert extra keyframes at scene cuts, which are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: GOP length in frames = keyframe interval in seconds x frame rate, the usual relation between an encoder's keyframe interval and its group-of-pictures setting
